title: feat(update): add optional SHA512 checksum and sidecar URLs
body:
SHA-512 API, precedence, sidecar parsing, and tests look good and correctly mirror the SHA-256 path.

Please address the FLASH always-link before merge like SHA-256.

comments.body:
This path (and `_sha512FreeContext()` from `_reset`/`begin`) lives in `Updater.cpp`, so `--gc-sections` cannot drop SHA-512.

That pulls `mbedtls_sha512_*` / `psa_hash_*` into every sketch that uses `Update`, including ones that never call `setSHA512()`. CI matches this: `SD_Update` (no TLS) grows about +5K FLASH on ESP32/C3/C6, +7K on C5/P4, and +11K on H2.

This also fights the SHA-256 comment at the top of this file: mbedtls SHA-256 was chosen specifically to avoid linking the SHA-512 software implementation into every Update sketch.

Please lazy-link SHA-512 the same way `HTTPUpdateChecksum.cpp` does (separate TU + function pointer assigned only from `setSHA512()`).

The heap context is on-demand, but FLASH is not. `_writeBuffer` / `_reset` always reference the SHA-512 helpers, so mbedtls/PSA SHA-512 is linked into every `Update` binary.

Please lazy-link SHA-512.

title: Add CI check for error_tags

comments.body:
`error_tags_check.yml` не перезапускается при добавлении `ok-to-test`, в отличие от `pr_check.yml`.

В `pr_check` явно указано:

```yaml
types:
  - opened
  - synchronize
  - reopened
  - labeled
```

В `error_tags_check` — только дефолтные события (`opened`, `synchronize`, `reopened`), без `labeled`.

**Что ломается:** для внешнего контрибьютора workflow стартует на `opened`, ownership check возвращает `false`, валидация skip'ается. Maintainer ставит `ok-to-test` → `pr_check` сразу перезапускается, а `error_tags_check` — нет, пока автор не сделает новый push.

**Предложение:** добавить `labeled` в `on.pull_request_target.types` (и по аналогии с `pr_check` — concurrency/условие, чтобы irrelevant labels не отменяли running checks).

title: Fix infinite layout loop caused by `desired_size` circular dependency
body:
The changes to `get_bound_desired_size()` and most of `Label` are mostly okay; however, the removal of the checks for `!is_expanded_by_desired_size()` causes `Label` outside of a `Container` to no longer expand up to its maximum size. 
I don't think removing these checks is necessary based on your PR description, so why did you remove them? 

dev4:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/12f28272-41e9-4173-905f-eeaaa41094fb

PR:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f789c1c-7cbc-4fad-a2af-aa58e08d428f

Also, "Desired size is an intrinsic property and shouldn't be capped by dynamic parent layout caches." is an incorrect statement, as it includes the desired height, which is computed by the `Control` based on the width it is given; hence, it is dynamic and not intrinsic. Only the desired width is an intrinsic property.

In the current state, all callers of `get_bound_desired_size` rely on their own clamping of children's sizes based on their maximum sizes, so the change is acceptable.

In the future, when the desired size is separated into its basic components and exposed to users, the height component will need to be reverted to clamping based on the combined maximum size. This is a discussion beyond the scope of this PR though, so I will leave it at that.

comments.body: Also, this should just replace the `combined_max` declaration above.
This is incorrect; please revert. The `maximum_width` variable also accounts for the stylebox's size, which reduces the effective maximum area for the text of the `Label`.

title: website/docs: document password lockout

comments.body:
```suggestion
A password locked user is restored in one of two ways:
```

```suggestion
- An administrator unlocks the user in **Directory** > **Users** and selects **Unlock password**.
```

```suggestion
Both clear the failure count, and unlocking created a `password_unlocked` event in the event log.
```

```suggestion
- **Failed attempts before cancel**: how many failed password submissions are allowed before the flow is canceled. This only ends the flow; the user can restart the flow immediately.
```

```suggestion
- **Failed attempts before lockout**: how many consecutive failed submissions password lock the user's account. Set to `0` to never password lock. Requires an enterprise license. See [Password lockout](#password-lockout).
```

We need to be careful to always say "password lock" rather than just "lock" because a user can still login via non password based flows.

```suggestion
Password locking is deliberately invisible to the person at the login prompt: the flow reports the same "Invalid password" error it reports for a wrong password, so the response cannot be used to discover whether an account exists or has been locked. The lock itself is recorded as a `password_locked` event in the [event log](../../../../sys-mgmt/events/index.md).
```
There should be a mention that this password locking doesn't affect passwordless flows.

title: feat(spans-buffer): add Redis slowlog logger for debugging
body:
I am not sure I understand what you would use the SLOWLOG response for. 
SLOWLOG tells you the  list of commands that took the longest in the previous period of time. 
If you want to use this to validate that the flusher is the cause of the CPU spikes, why not record the cumulative time  spent and amount of data extracted by each queue like we do for the cumulative time spent per trace ?

comments.body:
They would not. SLOWLOG is per Redis host (which means per shard). Actually I don't think calling it from the client will serve any purpose as the host you hit from the client may not be the one that serves the request. redis node can forward requests to other nodes if they do not own the shard that executes the command. 

So you would have to connect specifically to the shard that you are interested into and run the SLOWLOG command on there, otherwise you would be running it on the wrong node.
I don't think this will do what you want. SLOWLOG is per node on the cluster, not per cluster. It would give different results depending which node you run it onto.

title: Handle BadImageFormatException in OpenAssociatedSymbolFile
body:
Why do we want to mask this error? It does not look right to me. Our general strategy in AOT compilers is to fail the compilation when the input is malformed. It is expected that the malformed input can and will cause the compiler to crash or fail

The error in the issue is either a race condition in the build where the build is overwriting the compiler inputs, or it is a memory corruption (e.g. GC hole) leading to intermittent crash.

We need to get a crash dump of the failure to tell. It is a long outstanding problem that the builds are not producing crash dumps that made investigation of many issues difficult/impossible.
